target_customer: Residents and office workers in apartment and office buildings, sold through building owners and managers
problem: Convenience delivery is expensive per customer; Avo served a whole building at once through a branded in building online store.
business_model: Online convenience store and amenity platform for buildings, retail margin on goods and services delivered
product_category: Grocery and convenience delivery, building commerce

founders.name: Dekel Valtzer
prior_employers: monday.com (head of finance and operations, early employee)
founders.background_notes: Israel national tennis champion in 2005 and Davis Cup team member (Calcalist, 2021).

founders.name: Nir Smadar
founders.background_notes: From the YC page bio; Calcalist calls him VP Product.

exit.reason: Globes reported in May 2022 that Avo closed its Israeli activity and laid off its local operations staff after cutting about two thirds of staff; the company said residential delivery was too costly for a young startup. Aggregators date full cessation to 2024.

technical_complexity.rationale: A storefront app plus logistics and inventory operations; the difficulty was operations and unit economics, not engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Contracts with building owners gave some access, but delivery and inventory are copyable and Globes described the field as low gross margin.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying Avo; CEO Valtzer said the big grocers were not its true competitors, and Avo shrank in 2022 due to cost and cooler investment.

market_need_then: Valtzer described the idea as concentrated demand ('a lot of kids in one place'), starting with a kindergarten pilot in 2017 where teachers texted orders; Calcalist reported 1000% growth by Sept 2021.

branding.domain_note: Used avonow.com, a suffix domain rather than avo.com.

identity.voice_and_tone: CEO line: 'At Avo, you can order as little as a single avocado'

brand_strength.rationale: Calcalist (2021) noted Avo was not a familiar name to most Israeli consumers even though it served tens of thousands, because it sold through buildings rather than to consumers directly.

pivots.from: Residential and office building delivery in Israel and the US
pivots.to: Retreat to offices and companies, closing Israeli operations
pivots.why: Delivery to apartments was too costly and investment cooled (Globes)

outcome_analysis: Avo grew quickly after a 2017 kindergarten pilot and raised a 45 million dollar Series B in September 2021 on claimed 1000% growth. Delivery proved costly, with low gross margins, and when investment cooled in 2022 the company cut about two thirds of staff and closed its Israeli business in May 2022. Company databases later list it as ceased by 2024.
notes: Earlier funding: Calcalist says about 40 million dollars was raised before the Series B, and citybiz and pulse2 headlines say over 80 million in total; only the Series A is recorded and it rests on a single database (BounceWatch, 2018-11, Harlo Equity Partners and F2 Capital, amount undisclosed), while Startupim lists an undisclosed Series A in 2019-10, so dates conflict and 40 million of earlier funding is unaccounted for. Series B stated by Calcalist, Globes and Venture Capital Journal. Another YC page figure says over 100 million raised, which conflicts. Competitor list is empty because no source dated near the 2018 batch was found; the 2021 articles name Amazon, Walmart and Israeli grocers as the market, which is later than founding. Company website returned 503.
